questions.stem: The figure below has 8 sides. All its angles are right angles or 270°. Shu Fen counts the pairs of parallel sides (any two sides that lie on parallel lines count as a pair, and no two sides lie on the same line). How many pairs are there?

explain.why: Counted the pairs of the other kind.

solution: There are 4 horizontal-direction sides and 4 vertical-direction sides (perpendicular to each other).
Parallel pairs: each direction gives 4×3÷2 = 6 and 4×3÷2 = 6

questions.stem: How many of the nets A to D can be folded into a closed cube? (Kumar is checking each net.)

explain.why: Accepted a net where two faces overlap.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

questions.stem: Jun Wei draws the four nets A, B, C and D, each made of 6 squares. How many of them can be folded to make a cube without any overlap or gap?

explain.why: Accepted a net where two faces overlap.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

solution: Base has n sides: a prism has 3n edges, 2n vertices, n + 2 faces.

questions.stem: Aisha draws the four nets A, B, C and D, each made of 6 squares. How many of them can be folded to make a cube without any overlap or gap?

explain.why: Accepted a net where two faces overlap.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

questions.stem: Shu Fen's prism has 30 edges. How many faces does it have?

explain.why: Stopped at the number of sides of the base.

solution: Base has n sides: a prism has 3n edges, 2n vertices, n + 2 faces.

questions.stem: Four nets of six squares are shown. For how many of them will the squares fold up to form a cube? (Daniel is testing them.)

explain.why: Accepted a net where two faces overlap.

solution: A cube net needs 6 squares that fold with no two faces landing on the same side.
Rows of four squares with one square above and one below always work; a net with four squares in a row and both extras on the same side, or with a 2 × 2 block, fails.

questions.stem: Wei Jie draws a rectangle, then 3 lines across it parallel to the length and 2 lines parallel to the breadth, each from one side to the opposite side (see figure). Counting the four sides of the rectangle as lines too, how many pairs of perpendicular lines are there?

explain.why: Worked with the inner lines only.
Counted the pairs of the other kind.
Left out the sides of the rectangle.

solution: Lines parallel to the length: 3 + 2 = 5. Lines parallel to the breadth: 2 + 2 = 4.

questions.stem: On the square grid, A is at (4, 6) and B is at (5, 7). For how many of the points P, Q, R and S is the line joining the point to A perpendicular to AB?

explain.why: Counted the points that are not perpendicular.

solution: AB goes 1 across and 1 up. A perpendicular line goes 1 across and 1 the other way (or a multiple).

explain.why: Worked with the inner lines only.
Left out the sides of the rectangle.
Counted the pairs of the other kind.

solution: Lines parallel to the length: 4 + 2 = 6. Lines parallel to the breadth: 2 + 2 = 4.

questions.stem: Arjun has some identical blocks, each 2 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm. What is the smallest number of blocks needed to build a solid cube?

explain.why: Gave the edge of the cube.
Gave the volume of the cube.

solution: The edge of the cube must be a multiple of 2, 4 and 5: LCM = 20 cm

questions.stem: Priya paints all the outside faces of a cuboid 5 cm by 6 cm by 9 cm, then cuts it into 1 cm cubes. How many of the small cubes have exactly 2 faces painted?

explain.why: Counted the corner cubes in every edge.

solution: Each edge has (edge − 2) cubes with 2 painted faces; add over the 12 edges: 4 × (3 + 4 + 7) = 56
